content.title: About
content.content: Beef breakfast sausage is a pre‑cooked meat product that only needs reheating before eating. It has a rich meaty flavor, a hint of spices, and a tender texture, making it convenient for quick breakfasts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beef breakfast sausages often contain a blend of spices such as black pepper, paprika, and garlic.
Pre‑cooking reduces the final cooking time to just 2–3 minutes.
Beyond breakfast, the sausages can be added to salads, pastas, and casseroles.
They are especially popular in the United States and Canada, typically served with eggs and toast.
Some recipes include a small amount of sugar to balance the savory taste.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Beef sausage provides about 12–14 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from beef helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels and energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12 and niacin, important for the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Pre‑cooking makes the proteins more readily digestible.

items.title: Convenient and fast
items.content: Quick reheating provides a nutritious breakfast without lengthy preparation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Sausages often contain high levels of salt, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some products use nitrites and other preservatives that should be limited.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Due to fat content, sausages are relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reheat the sausage in a pan, microwave, or simmering water for 2–3 minutes. Serve with eggs, toast, vegetables, or add to omelets and salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at +2…+4 °C in the original packaging for up to 5 days after opening. Freeze at ‑18 °C for longer storage (up to 3 months).
